• Xylem consists of tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres.
• Tracheids and vessels have thick walls, and many are dead cells when mature.

Sieve tubes are tubular cells with perforated walls.
Phloem transports food from leaves to other parts of the plant.

BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):
- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the result first (what it makes). 2) inputs and the place. 3) each step with its cause and its condition. 4) what breaks when a step fails. 5) the whole run once more at speed. 6) recap as a flow.
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the whole in context. 2) zoom into each part in a fixed path (outside to inside). 3) function of each part tied to its shape. 4) how the parts work together. 5) labelled recap.
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the overview tree first: the basis of division and every member named. 2) every member in the same slots: layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence. 3) the members compared side by side, the most confused pair named directly. 4) a memory trick for the family.
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what is common. 2) criteria one at a time, both sides together. 3) the reason behind each difference. 4) the most confused pair named directly. 5) difference table as recap.
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the period and its atmosphere. 2) events in order with their causes. 3) the people and their choices. 4) the turning point. 5) what changed after. 6) timeline recap.
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the effect students can see. 2) the cause. 3) each link of the chain with its mechanism. 4) the evidence. 5) the exception or limit. 6) the chain as recap.
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the fact in one line. 2) the number shown to scale against something familiar. 3) where it comes from (book or outside, dated). 4) what it changes or proves. 5) a formula built term by term when there is one.
- figure · Figure: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only). Required questions: what (kya), which (kaun). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what the figure is and why it is here. 2) a reading path across it (labels in order). 3) the one thing to remember from it. 4) link back to the text it explains.
- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) a concrete example first. 2) the book's definition word by word. 3) a non-example that tests the boundary. 4) where the term is used next in the chapter.

Level profile: UPSC / State PCS (level_profiles.json; learners: UPSC and State PCS aspirants, often from arts backgrounds, who need understanding more than technical vocabulary).
- Terms: fewer technical terms: only the ones the exam asks, each opened with its plain meaning and an everyday image; a term the exam never asks is explained in words, not named.
- Why: 2 step(s); a two-step why from a need the learner can feel, then its link to daily life, health or governance.
- Where found: the main places, each linked to something the learner already knows (a disease, a food, a news item).
- Exam beats: the PYQ pattern: how this fact has been asked (statement combinations, 'which is correct', odd one out) and the wording that traps.
- Links: daily life, health, the news and earlier chapters of the same paper.

How real teachers open a book line (teacher example bank 2026-10-24.1; use these ways, in your own words):
- Open with a question on something visible (every new topic and every new family member): Skin aur stomach, kidney ke upar ek outer layer hai ki nahi? Yeh kis se bani hai? — phir naam: epithelial tissue.
- One everyday image per shape or function (every term that names a shape, a layer or a job): Chaadar bichhi ho to bistar bacha rehta hai = protective sheet. Cube wala game, har side barabar = cuboidal. Building ka pillar = columnar. Farsh ki tiles = squamous, isliye tessellated bhi kehte hain.
- The word root where it helps (a term whose parts carry its meaning): Epi yaani upar; epithelium yaani upar ki parat. Slender yaani long aur narrow.
- Why starts from a need (every why step): Pet mein HCl banta hai, isliye andar ek lining chahiye jo khud na jale. Cells bahar ki taraf hain, tootne ka chance zyada, isliye regeneration zyada.
- Contrast with the neighbour (members of one family, and what the exam confuses): Simple epithelium ka kaam protection nahi, woh compound ka hai. Zyada layers = pathogen andar nahi aata.
- Ask and repeat the key word (the one word the learner must keep): Irregular walls. Kaisi? Irregular.
- Exam memory beats by level (after the understanding, by the level profile): Yaad rakhna: brush border PCT mein. Doosre naam: pavement, tessellated. M2B = muscle to bone = tendon, B2B = bone to bone = ligament.
- Link to something already known (a new place or a new structure): Peritoneum, jaise lungs ke aas-paas pleura aur heart ke aas-paas pericardium: wahi kaam, pet ke andar.
- Meaning with two or three real examples (an abstract word in the book): Sensory perception yaani pehchanna: thanda lagna, dard hona, pressure mehsoos karna.
- Open the book's adjective (Navin's example) (a book line names a kind of surface, job or place without saying what it is): Book: 'epithelium absorptive aur secretive surfaces par milta hai'. Teacher: absorptive surface yaani jahan cheezein andar li jaati hain, jaise aant khane ke poshak tatva sokhti hai; secretive yaani jahan cells kuch bana kar bahar chhodte hain, jaise glands enzyme ya juice. Aur epithelium wahan kyon? Kyunki ek patli, lagi hui parat hi cheezon ko paar jaane de sakti hai aur bana kar chhod sakti hai.

Brackets (word list 2026-10-25.1): use everyday spoken Hindi freely, without brackets (मुख्य, वापस, बराबर, आसपास, इस्तेमाल, करके, जिससे ...). Only a genuinely difficult Hindi word (formal, literary or technical) gets its English word in brackets right after it, for example "सतह (surface)", "घर्षण (friction)", "सघन (dense)"; better still, use the book's English term or a simpler Hindi word. Never put a bracket inside an idiom or a fixed phrase: "आम तौर पर", not "आम तौर (usually) पर"; "नहीं के बराबर", not "नहीं के बराबर (equal to)". Video v9: Xylem और phloem: components से transport समझें
Goal: आप complex tissue का मतलब, xylem और phloem के सभी components, उनके काम, labelled drawings और stem arrangement समझेंगे; living–dead exceptions तथा non-xylem component question सही करेंगे।
Opening hook: जड़ों से पानी और पत्तियों से बना food बाकी plant तक पहुँचता है—क्या दोनों के लिए एक जैसी transport line होती है?
Story or analogy: Transport network का visual अलग materials और routes समझाने में मदद करेगा; storage तथा support करने वाले components को भी दिखाएँगे, ताकि हर component को केवल pipe न मानें।
Planned minutes: 12
Narration time (S2-01): 9.5-12.7 minutes, about 1235-1651 spoken words (BIE counts 130 words a minute)
Prerequisites already taught in the prerequisite video (remind of one in at most 2 beats): Cell boundaries, organelles and plant–animal cell differences; Chromosomes, homologous pairs, chromatids, DNA replication and chromosome sets; Somatic cells, germ cells, gametes and fertilisation; Locations and roles of the named human organs, passages and skeleton; Plant organ landmarks and sections; Diffusion, absorption, secretion and movement through walls or pores; Photosynthesis, food storage and the functions of structural biological materials; Physical meanings of tension, elasticity, pressure, buoyancy and insulation; Stimulus, nerve impulse, electrical signal and voluntary versus involuntary control
Open every book line (S2-07): a question about something the learner can see, then the name; every term opened: its plain meaning with 'yaani' and one everyday image (the word root where it helps); the why, starting from a need or a problem, one link at a time; an example or the place, by a zoom from the organ or the thing the learner knows; the consequence: what follows, and the link to the previous or the next idea; the contrast: what it is not, and what the exam confuses it with; the memory beat by level: the exam's 'yaad rakhna', the other names, the trick.

frame.process: Complex tissue combines different cell types; xylem combines conducting, storage and supporting components.
frame.how: Read the tissue assembly, then its four components and the walls and interiors of its conducting elements.
frame.when: Mature conducting elements are distinguished from developing cells.
frame.conditions: An open conducting space and reinforced walls support conduction; living parenchyma qualifies whole-tissue dead-cell claims.
frame.atmosphere: Picture a stem transport network with conduits, neighbouring storage cells and reinforcing fibres.

frame.process: Complex tissues distribute supplies; xylem combines vertical conduction, sideways transfer, storage and support.
frame.how: Connect separated supply and demand locations to tubular conducting elements, parenchyma and fibres.
frame.when: Supplies move as plant parts require them; the explanation follows need, route and associated functions.
frame.conditions: Tube shape provides a route, not the complete force driving upward movement.
frame.atmosphere: Follow water from roots through a stem, then toward neighbouring tissues.

frame.process: Complex permanent tissues are grouped as xylem and phloem.
frame.how: Distinguish their principal cargo while retaining their shared organisation of cooperating cell types.
frame.when: Introduce the family before studying individual components.
frame.conditions: The division concerns tissue identity and principal transport role, not identical cells.
frame.atmosphere: Picture parallel water-supply and food-distribution networks in one plant.

frame.process: Phloem includes five named component types with different roles.
frame.how: Move from conducting cells to companion cells, fibres and parenchyma, then compare their jobs.
frame.when: Read this as a general component list, not compulsory coexistence of all five in every plant.
frame.conditions: Sieve cells and sieve tubes are different conducting forms.
frame.atmosphere: Zoom into food-conducting tissue in a stem.

frame.process: Sieve-tube elements form a food-conducting tube with perforated connecting end regions.
frame.how: Zoom from phloem to the tube, its element walls and sieve plates.
frame.when: Successive elements connect along the conducting route.
frame.conditions: Perforated does not mean unrestricted holes throughout every wall.
frame.atmosphere: Imagine joined pipe sections with sieve-like connecting plates.

frame.process: Phloem distributes leaf-made food and is living apart from the stated fibre exception.
frame.how: State each fact, locate its supporting text and explain its consequence.
frame.when: Food goes to consuming or storage regions; mature fibres are the living-cell exception.
frame.conditions: Neither downward-only transport nor all-cells-living is a valid absolute.
frame.atmosphere: Follow food from a leaf toward growing plant parts.

skipped_steps.why: These are qualitative facts without a numerical quantity to show to scale.

frame.process: The drawings identify whole-tissue components and enlarged conducting-cell details.
frame.how: Read the upper pair left to right, then the lower isolated and grouped xylem and phloem views.
frame.when: Move from the overview to individual elements and their grouped arrangement.
frame.conditions: Leader lines identify parts, colours are illustrative, and an unclear pointer cannot establish an exact target.
frame.atmosphere: Inspect labelled drawings as identification evidence rather than flow diagrams.

frame.process: Compare xylem and phloem across cargo, living condition, walls, permeability, materials and support.
frame.how: Take one criterion at a time and explain the limits of the printed shorthand.
frame.when: Compare after both component families and their drawings are understood.
frame.conditions: Component-level exceptions prevent absolute interpretations of the table.
frame.atmosphere: Place the two transport networks side by side in the same plant.

frame.process: A stem region is enlarged to locate xylem, cambium and phloem and show transport arrows.
frame.how: Read outer landmarks, centre, vascular positions and then the magnified longitudinal view.
frame.when: The red arrow changes viewing scale; black arrows depict movement.
frame.conditions: The arrangement belongs to the illustrated stem; downward phloem arrows are not a universal direction rule.
frame.atmosphere: Zoom from a stem segment into its conducting region.

frame.process: Identify the option that does not belong to xylem.
frame.how: Read except, classify each option and explain why parenchyma remains a valid xylem component.
frame.when: Attempt after learning both tissue families.
frame.conditions: Shared transport functions do not imply shared component membership.
frame.atmosphere: A supplied multiple-choice practice question; no examination provenance is assumed.

beats.say: जड़ों का पानी पत्तियों तक और पत्तियों का खाना बाकी plant तक कैसे पहुँचता है? क्या दोनों की transport line एक है?
beats.on_screen: Plant with root-water and leaf-food supply routes.

beats.say: इन रास्तों के नाम क्या हैं? Permanent tissue की complex शाखा में Xylem और Phloem हैं; दोनों अलग cells की transport teams हैं।
beats.on_screen: Permanent → complex → Xylem / Phloem.

beats.say: जड़ से ऊपर जाती line कौन है? Xylem, यानी water और minerals का रास्ता; लंबे conducting cells के साथ storage और support वाले cells भी हैं।
beats.on_screen: Xylem route through root, stem and leaf.

beats.say: पत्ती का खाना कौन बाँटेगा? Phloem, यानी food delivery वाली team; इसकी लंबी conducting line के साथ helper, storage और support cells हैं।
beats.on_screen: Food route from leaves to consuming regions.

beats.say: फर्क सामान का है: Xylem में water-minerals, Phloem में food। दोनों complex हैं, क्योंकि अलग cells मिलकर काम करते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Cargo contrast; shared complex organisation.

beats.say: याद रखने की तस्वीर: Xylem की water line, Phloem की food delivery; हर line के पीछे cells की team है।
beats.on_screen: Water line / food delivery.

beats.say: एक tissue में अलग cells क्यों दिखते हैं? Complex tissue में कई cell types coordinate करते हैं, जैसे रसोई की team; simple tissue में मुख्य type एक जैसा था।
beats.on_screen: Different cells inside one tissue boundary.

beats.say: Xylem की team कौन है? Tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma और xylem fibres। ऊपर चारों labelled हैं; नीचे conducting elements और parenchyma बड़े करके दिखाए हैं।
beats.on_screen: Four components; upper and lower views.

beats.say: मोटी walls क्यों? Mature, यानी पूरी तरह तैयार, tracheids और vessels में अंदर खाली रास्ता पानी ले जाता है; मजबूत walls दबकर बंद होने से बचाती हैं। Book कई mature cells को dead कहती है।
beats.on_screen: Thick wall around an empty conducting space.

beats.say: Conductors पानी ले जाते हैं, parenchyma storage और sideways transfer करता है, fibres सहारा देते हैं। पूरा xylem dead नहीं: parenchyma living है।
beats.on_screen: Conduct / store and transfer / support.

beats.say: Drawings में यही complex organisation पहचानो: अलग cells, साझा काम। Xylem किसी अकेले cell का नाम नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Labelled xylem and phloem teams.

beats.say: दूर बैठे plant parts को सामान कैसे मिलेगा? Complex tissues transport करते हैं, यानी water, minerals और food को जरूरत वाली जगह पहुँचाते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Supply linked to demand.

beats.say: जड़ों से पानी-minerals मिलते हैं, पत्तियों में खाना बनता है। बाकी हिस्सों को supply चाहिए; Xylem पानी और Phloem food पहुँचाता है।
beats.on_screen: Different supply locations and routes.

beats.say: लंबी नली से क्या काम होता है? Tubular tracheids और vessels water-minerals को vertically, यानी लंबाई में ऊपर, रास्ता देते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Trace the longitudinal conducting route.

beats.say: बगल के cells तक पानी कैसे पहुँचे? Xylem parenchyma sideways conduction करता है, जैसे मुख्य line की शाखा; food भी store करता है।
beats.on_screen: Vertical route with lateral branch and storage.

beats.say: ढाँचा कौन थामेगा? Xylem fibres mainly supportive हैं; मोटी, lignified walls सहारा देती हैं, जैसे line के साथ मजबूत brace।
beats.on_screen: Fibres reinforce conduits.

beats.say: इस division के सबूत बताए गए काम हैं: ऊपर conduction, बगल में distribution और fibres से support। केवल लंबी line पूरी जरूरत नहीं समझाती।
beats.on_screen: Evidence: three distinct component functions.

beats.say: लेकिन tube केवल रास्ता है, पानी चढ़ने की पूरी वजह नहीं। Transpiration pull और पानी का आपसी जुड़ाव भी जरूरी हैं।
beats.on_screen: Route is not the driving force.

beats.say: Chain जोड़ो: दूर की supply के लिए conductors, बगल की supply और storage के लिए parenchyma, मजबूती के लिए fibres।
beats.on_screen: Need → route / distribution / reinforcement.

beats.say: Food delivery की team में कौन हैं? Phloem में sieve cells, sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem fibres और phloem parenchyma हैं; जैसे delivery में रास्ता, helper और भंडार चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Five-component phloem tree linked to delivery roles.

beats.say: लंबे conductors देखो: sieve cells और sieve tubes अलग forms हैं। Sieve छन्नी जैसा है; हर plant में दोनों साथ होना जरूरी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Separate conducting forms, not compulsory coexistence.

beats.say: Tube के पास पतला साथी कौन है? Companion cell, यानी helper; slender मतलब लंबा-पतला, building के pillar जैसा। यह tube और sugar transfer में मदद करता है।
beats.on_screen: Slender companion cell beside tube.

beats.say: रस्सी जैसे हिस्से कौन हैं? Phloem fibres support देते हैं। पास के phloem parenchyma storage cells हैं, जैसे delivery route का भंडार।
beats.on_screen: Support fibres and storage parenchyma.

beats.say: Sieve tube रास्ता है, companion cell helper; दोनों एक नहीं। Parenchyma storage और fibre support करता है, केवल पास होने से काम एक नहीं होता।
beats.on_screen: Compare the four roles.

beats.say: याद रखो: 2 conducting नाम, फिर helper, सहारा और भंडार। इसी तस्वीर से phloem के 5 components जोड़ो।
beats.on_screen: Two conductors + helper + support + storage.

beats.say: जुड़ी नली की बीच वाली दीवार बंद हो तो रस कैसे निकलेगा? Phloem की sieve tube में छन्नी जैसे जोड़ रास्ता देते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Phloem tube with open connecting end regions.

beats.say: Tubular यानी pipe जैसा लंबा; perforated यानी छोटे छेद वाला। छन्नी जैसे end-wall जोड़ को देखो, हर wall में छेद मत मानना।
beats.on_screen: Zoom into perforated end region.

beats.say: रस को अगले cell तक जाना है; इसलिए sieve plate के openings बंद दीवार के बजाय गुजरने का रास्ता देते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Sap passes through plate openings.

beats.say: Elements सिरों से जुड़ें और plates रस गुजरने दें, तो अलग cells मिलकर लंबी food line बना देते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Assemble tube from successive elements.

beats.say: Labels जोड़ो: phloem में tube, tube की cell-unit element, और units के बीच plate। Plate अलग cell type नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Tissue → tube → element → plate.

beats.say: बढ़ती जड़ को खाना कौन देगा? Phloem पत्ती से food पहुँचाता है, जैसे रसोई से delivery। Living cells वाली इसकी पहचान में fibres exception हैं।
beats.on_screen: Leaf-food delivery; fibre exception.

beats.say: Page की table भी leaves से growing parts तक food बताती है। अलग exception-line, fibres को छोड़कर living cells कहती है; broad table को इससे जोड़कर पढ़ो।
beats.on_screen: Link table and exception line.

beats.say: नतीजा: food बनाने और इस्तेमाल की जगहें अलग हो सकती हैं। Fibres की मजबूत walls dead होने पर भी सहारा देती हैं; ‘सभी phloem cells living’ गलत है।
beats.on_screen: Distribution need and living-cell exception.

beats.say: कौन-सी line नाम पहचानाती है? ऊपर left Xylem, right Phloem है; leaders flow नहीं बताते। नीचे individual और grouped views details खोलते हैं; a-b views हैं।
beats.on_screen: Overview and enlarged views; leader-line legend.

beats.say: ऊपर Xylem Parenchyma storage और sideways supply करता है। चौड़ा Vessels वाला हिस्सा ऊपर जाता रास्ता है, लंबी पानी की line जैसा।
beats.on_screen: Upper xylem: parenchyma, vessels.

beats.say: लंबे Tracheids भी vessels जैसे water-minerals ऊपर ले जाते हैं। Xylem Fibres सहारा हैं, जैसे line के साथ brace; ये conductor का दूसरा नाम नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Upper tracheids and supporting fibres.

beats.say: Right में Phloem Parenchyma पहचानो। Tube के पास Companion cell slender है, यानी लंबा-पतला, सीधे pillar जैसा पड़ोसी helper।
beats.on_screen: Phloem parenchyma and slender companion cell.

beats.say: Phloem fibres रस्सी जैसे सहारे हैं; xylem में भी fibres थे। बड़ी Sieve tube खाना पहुँचाने की नली है, बगल में companion helper है।
beats.on_screen: Fibres as reinforcing cords; sieve tube and adjacent companion cell.

beats.say: नीचे pink vessel element vessel की 1 unit है। Pitted walls में पतली खिड़कियों जैसी जगहें exchange देती हैं; पूरी तरह खाली छेद नहीं हैं।
beats.on_screen: Isolated vessel element; pit magnification.

beats.say: पतले होते सिरों वाले cells tracheids हैं। Grey xylem parenchyma cell slender, यानी लंबा-पतला pillar जैसा है; storage और sideways water transfer करता है।
beats.on_screen: Tapered tracheids and grey parenchyma.

beats.say: Group का vessel element पानी आगे पहुँचाने वाला pipe का टुकड़ा है। Pitted walls, यानी पतली खिड़कियों जैसी जगहें, बगल में पानी जाने देती हैं; अकेले element में भी इन्हें पहचानो।
beats.on_screen: Match the grouped vessel element to the isolated view; magnify thinner pit regions and show lateral water exchange through remaining membranes.

beats.say: नीचे tracheid label xylem का है; pointer साफ नहीं, इसलिए खास cell नहीं चुनेंगे। Shape साफ isolated view से सीखो।
beats.on_screen: Unclear pointer retained without an invented target.

beats.say: Blue cell sieve-tube element, यानी tube की 1 unit है। End की sieve plate छन्नी जैसा जोड़ है, जिससे रस अगले element में जाता है।
beats.on_screen: Isolated element and end plate.

beats.say: पड़ोसी companion cell का dark nucleus काम सँभालने वाले office जैसा है। Mature sieve-tube element बिना nucleus भी living है; उसका helper पास रहकर काम सँभालता है।
beats.on_screen: Companion nucleus as a coordinating office; mature sieve-tube element lacks a nucleus.

beats.say: अकेले view के phloem parenchyma भंडार वाले साथी हैं। Group में companion cell tube के बगल में दिखता है, जैसे helper; plate का हिस्सा नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Parenchyma label; companion association across views.

beats.say: Group का चौड़ा blue cell sieve-tube element है। बीच की sieve plate छन्नी जैसा दरवाजा है; अकेले view के end पर भी यही जोड़ था।
beats.on_screen: Grouped element and transverse connecting plate.

beats.say: Group के phloem parenchyma, companion और tube अलग cells हैं। Plasmodesmata पड़ोसी living cells के बीच छोटे connecting रास्ते हैं, जिनसे चीज़ें और signals जा सकते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Parenchyma label and fine plasmo-desmata connections.

beats.say: मुख्य पहचान रखो: xylem के vessels-tracheids और phloem के elements-plates रास्ते दिखाते हैं। Conducting cell, wall feature और पड़ोसी cell अलग चीज़ें हैं।
beats.on_screen: Cell / wall feature / associated cell.

beats.say: Text की team drawing में दिख गई: conductor के साथ storage, helper या support। Labels पहचान बताते हैं, flow नहीं; केवल रंग से फैसला मत करना।
beats.on_screen: Link labelled components to text functions.

beats.say: दोनों lines में common क्या है? दोनों complex transport tissues हैं; अब table को components के फर्क के साथ पढ़ेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Shared organisation above comparison table.

beats.say: जड़ों की supply water-minerals है: Xylem उसे leaves तक ले जाता है। पत्ती रसोई जैसी है; Phloem वहाँ का food growing parts तक पहुँचाता है। पहचान सामान से करो।
beats.on_screen: Root water supply versus leaf kitchen and food delivery.

beats.say: Table में xylem dead, thick-walled; phloem living, thin-walled है। Exceptions लगाओ: living xylem parenchyma और dead, thick-walled phloem fibres।
beats.on_screen: Living condition and thickness with exceptions.

beats.say: Table xylem को water-impermeable, phloem को food-permeable कहती है। Pipe की wall पानी रोके, भीतर रास्ता उसे ले जाए: दोनों बातें अलग हैं; यह simplified wording है।
beats.on_screen: Across-wall resistance versus flow inside lumen.

beats.say: Materials में lignin बनाम cellulose लिखा है। Cellulose wall का ढाँचा, कपास जैसा; lignin लकड़ी जैसी मजबूती जोड़ता है। Xylem में भी cellulose है।
beats.on_screen: Cellulose wall reinforced with lignin.

beats.say: Table xylem को mechanical strength देती है, phloem को नहीं। यानी भार-झुकाव सहना; मगर phloem fibres सहारा देते हैं, इसलिए यह absolute नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Support contrast qualified by phloem fibres.

beats.say: वजह जोड़ो: खाली xylem passage पानी ले जाता है; मोटी lignified walls collapse रोकती और plant को सहारा देती हैं। Dead होना रास्ता बंद होना नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Open passage + reinforced wall → conduction and strength.

beats.say: Confused pair पकड़ो: wall और अंदर का रास्ता अलग हैं। Living tissue का मतलब हर cell living नहीं; phloem transfer भी controlled है, खुला leakage नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Reject whole-tissue absolutes and unrestricted leakage.

beats.say: इन 6 rows में cargo, living condition, thickness, permeability, material और support पढ़ो। साथ में exceptions रखो; exam में ‘all’ और ‘only’ जाँचो।
beats.on_screen: Six-row comparison table with qualifications.

beats.say: Stem में ये lines कहाँ हैं? Red arrow camera के zoom जैसा vascular हिस्सा बड़ा दिखाता है: left xylem, बीच cambium, right phloem; यह flow नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Red magnification arrow from stem to vascular view.

beats.say: बाहरी छिलके जैसी परत कौन है? Epidermis। उसके नीचे cortex है, यानी vascular region से बाहर वाली पट्टी।
beats.on_screen: Outside-in: epidermis, cortex.

beats.say: बीच का हिस्सा क्या है? Pith, यानी centre। Vascular region की बीच वाली पट्टी cambium है; नई cells बनाती है, xylem-phloem के बीच रहती है।
beats.on_screen: Central pith and intervening cambium.

beats.say: Pith से अंदर-बाहर पहचानो: उसकी तरफ xylem की water-mineral line है। बाहर phloem की food-delivery line है, जैसे साथ चलती अलग services।
beats.on_screen: Inner xylem and outer phloem in illustrated stem.

beats.say: Enlargement में left xylem की मजबूत tubes में arrows ऊपर जाते हैं। बीच की cambium पट्टी divider जैसी है: left xylem, right phloem।
beats.on_screen: Upward xylem arrows and central cambium bracket.

beats.say: Right phloem के छन्नी जैसे ends और नीचे जाते arrows देखो। नीचे केवल यहाँ दिखाई direction है; food की जरूरत ऊपर हो तो transport ऊपर भी हो सकता है।
beats.on_screen: Perforated ends; downward arrows labelled illustrated case.

beats.say: इस stem में अंदर xylem, बीच cambium, बाहर phloem है। Red arrow camera के zoom जैसा है; black arrows रास्ते पर चलते सामान जैसे movement दिखाते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Spatial order; camera-zoom analogy for red arrow and cargo movement for black arrows.

beats.say: Outer covering-cortex और central pith से location मिली। अंदर water tubes और food वाले sieve-जोड़, text के structure और function को जोड़ते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Whole stem linked to enlarged transport structures.

beats.say: इन options में xylem का हिस्सा कौन नहीं है? ‘Except’ वाले question का answer A, Companion cells है: ये phloem के helpers हैं। Tracheid और vessel पानी के रास्ते हैं; xylem parenchyma storage और sideways transfer करता है।
beats.on_screen: Show all four supplied options; underline EXCEPT; select A.

beats.say: पूरी तस्वीर: complex tissue team है, केवल pipe नहीं। Xylem water-minerals, phloem food पहुँचाता है; components और exceptions पहचानकर drawing तथा statement questions हल करो।
beats.on_screen: Team → cargo → components → exceptions → identification.

notes.about: This unit covers complex permanent tissues (xylem and phloem), their cellular constituents, functional mechanisms, anatomical diagrams, cross-sectional stem arrangement, and comparative properties for UPSC/State PCS aspirants.
key_questions: What distinguishes complex permanent tissue from simple permanent tissue?
What are the specific components and functional adaptations of xylem and phloem?
Which components are living versus dead, and what are the classic exam exceptions?
How are xylem and phloem oriented in a young dicot stem cross-section relative to pith and epidermis?
How to avoid common multiple-choice traps regarding cell walls, permeability, and companion cells?

decisions.decision: Use kitchen delivery and plumbing analogies to distinguish bidirectional food translocation from largely unidirectional sap ascent.
decisions.reason: Arts-background aspirants grasp functional differences between vascular tissues intuitively when related to household utility systems.

decisions.decision: Carefully qualify broad textbook claims (such as 'xylem is dead' and 'phloem has no mechanical support') with explicit component exceptions.
decisions.reason: UPSC and State PCS statement-based questions frequently test 'all/none' absolute statements against exceptions like living xylem parenchyma and dead phloem fibres.
